AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim as that section binds every batch. The sim has no add-to-room phase - creature creation IS construction - so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (gremlin_merc.py:34-39). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set - the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on target is self.player / applier is self.player / card is not None, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire; sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion - the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering - MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) before the subclass applies its powers, but `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: every initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7 NOTE: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash, exactly as the seam records disclose. Payload and ORDER match: SurprisePower 1 then ThieveryPower 20 (GremlinMerc.cs:49-55 vs gremlin_merc.py:38-39). ESCALATION CHECK, because section 2 requires one when the C# body reads combat state: GremlinMerc.cs:50 iterates `Creature.CombatState.Players` and gives each player its own ThieveryPower instance with `Target = player.Creature`. That is a read of the PLAYER list, not of `enemies`, and it is multiplayer-only shape: the Ironclad-only sim has exactly one player, so the loop yields exactly one instance and the sim's single untargeted ThieveryPower (gremlin_merc.py:39, stolen through self.powers['thievery'] at :42-44) is the same object count with the same amount. The sim's __init__ reads no hooks.combat list at all, so the not-yet-assigned-enemies hazard section 2 names does not arise.

guards.what: Steal runs after the attack on all three moves
guards.rationale: GremlinMerc.cs:83-92, :99-108, :114-121 all await the Attack, then loop GetPowerInstances<ThieveryPower>() calling Steal(), and only THEN apply the move's rider (Weak on DoubleSmash, Strength on Hehe). gremlin_merc.py:67-83 uses the same order on all three. This is a real ordering question (PROMPT.md class 1): stealing before the attack would change the gold a lethal hit leaves behind.

The sim's _steal (gremlin_merc.py:41-44) reads the single self.powers['thievery']. Same set in single-player. guards.what: Death spawns are SurprisePower's, and their order matches
guards.rationale: The Sneaky/Fat spawn is not a GremlinMerc override - it is SurprisePower.AfterDeath (SurprisePower.cs:18-38), which adds SneakyGremlin into slot 'sneaky' then FatGremlin into slot 'fat'. Checked here because slot placement is the mechanism this batch found broken for LivingFog: GremlinMercNormal does NOT override EncounterModel.Slots (GremlinMercNormal.cs has only three unused const strings; the base default is Array.Empty<string>(), EncounterModel.cs:176), so CombatState.SortEnemiesBySlotName (CombatState.cs:495-501) compares Slots.IndexOf(...) = -1 against -1 for every pair and leaves the list in add order. The sim's SurprisePower appends in the same order (powers.py:1704-1706), so the enemy list agrees. NOT the same site as monster/living_fog's G1 - stated here so the two records' different verdicts on 'spawn ordering' are visibly about two different encounters (rule 3).

All 29 PROMPT.md bug classes checked against this unit. Class 6: no branch state. Class 10 (reset timing): the only per-combat field is _hasSpoken, presentation. Class 21 (death is not removal): the merc's death is a real death; SurprisePower.ShouldStopCombatFromEnding (SurprisePower.cs:40-43) keeps the combat alive but does not veto removal, and the sim's retained_after_death is not set for it. Class 25 (two-pass dispatchers): none of the merc's own moves dispatch a hook twice.
